definition: The case groups simple, perfect, good, one, infinite, immutable, eternal, intellect and will in the order of ClassicalAttributesSuffice. In the complete stage-2 composition its arguments are IsSimple Composite (DEF-SIMPLE), IsPerfect InAct (DEF-UNIVERSALLY-PERFECT), IsSupremelyGood InAct GoodIn CausesIn esse (DEF-SUPREMELY-GOOD), IsTheOneGod σ.IsGod (DEF-ONE-GOD), Infinite (DEF-INFINITE), IsImmutable InPotency (DEF-IMMUTABLE), Eternal (DEF-ETERNAL), HasIntellect (DEF-HAS-INTELLECT), and HasWill (DEF-HAS-WILL).
note: The owner's stage-2 reading of Dei Filius ch. 1. Signature.HasClassicalAttributes is still a primitive field. ClassicalAttributesSuffice is an explicit open, one-way premise from the nine predicates to that field, not a definitional equality or an eliminator recovering all nine predicates from it. GodHasClassicalAttributes means ∀ g, σ.IsGod g → σ.HasClassicalAttributes g. No changed proof, closed frontier, or truth of the bridge is claimed by adding this mapping.
